rationale: A defensible additive combination of the archive's two strongest conditioners on an unchanged yield leg, but it is incremental engineering rather than a new mechanism, and the equal-rank sum will be highly correlated with each parent signal.

The differenced ratio is dimensionally incoherent (cash is a stock share, depreciation an annual flow rate, with cash typically the larger and far more dispersed term), so after IND_RANK it will be close to a monotone relabeling of the already-tested cash-intensity conditioner rather than the claimed "single economic quantity."

MIN is a genuinely non-linear alternative to the additive form and matches the stated necessary-conditions logic, though the archive already shows conjunctive MIN gating tends to shrink dispersion and dilute alpha relative to the single-conditioner parents.

This is the sharpest proposal in the batch: it pits two competing interpretations of the cash result against each other with opposite predicted outcomes, and is informative either way, with the caveat that cash entering both the conditioner and the denominator makes some mechanical reinforcement unavoidable and worth acknowledging in the diagnosis.

Testing liquidity net of the claims against it is an economically sensible refinement of the cash conditioner with clean bounded construction, though it partly overlaps the already-tested low-leverage conditioner and needs a stated handling of the zero-cash/zero-debt undefined case.

The nesting gives cash 50% and the other two 25% each, contradicting the stated "equally weighted rank index," and stacking a five-year average ROA conditioner onto a five-year average operating profit yield is largely a kitchen-sink re-aggregation of already-tested components rather than a new economic test.
